messages:
Maria (support): customer reported large p99 jump for text/generate at ~11:02 UTC, multiple requests 5-10s. customer says it started suddenly and affects their UI. attaching sample request and span ids.
Theo (oncall): looking. any errors in traces or 503s?
Maria (support): logs show backpressure messages, admission queue length spiking. sample span id: trace/0a1b2c. No 5xx from backend aside from throttling.
Ben (eng-runtime): thanks — can you paste the curl we should repro with? also which region/tenant?
Maria (support): tenant acme-inc, region us-west-2. repro curl: 
```
curl -sS -X POST https://api.redwood.ai/v1/generate \ 
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN" \ 
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \ 
  -d '{"model":"open-rl-3b","input":"summarize: ...","max_tokens":256}'
```
Ben (eng-runtime): tried a quick run from a dev box, got a 200 but tail latency 3.2s. hitting /metrics shows worker_queue_length ~ 420 and inflight per-worker at 64 (limit 64). looks like admission control is fully saturated.
Alice (eng-sre): interesting — did autoscale trigger? I see reserved-worker-count unchanged, scaling cooldowns active. There was a deploy 10m before spike.
Theo (oncall): can we rollback that deploy to sanity-check?
Ben (eng-runtime): I can flip routing to previous revision for acme-inc only (canary rollback). Doing traffic-split change now to route 100% back to v2026.
ingest-bot: deploy-router: traffic update job queued (job id rtr-8172).
Maria (support): pinging customer: "we're routing you to an earlier model revision while we investigate — should be transparent"
Ben (eng-runtime): traffic switch complete. monitoring... queue length dropped to 30 in ~40s, p99 back to ~600ms.
Alice (eng-sre): root cause likely a combination: the new runtime kernel in v2027 increased per-request memory, reduced concurrent internal batching efficiency -> per-worker throughput dropped and admission pileup happened. We'll open a bug.
Theo (oncall): short-term mitigation: keep acme on v2026, increase admission queue limit by 20% for best-effort tenants? risks?
Ben (eng-runtime): increasing queue limit buys time but may increase latency and OOM risk. recommend autoscale aggressive policy for the affected pool + rollback for customers with urgent SLAs.
Maria (support): customer confirmed UI improved after the switch. they'll keep us posted if they see recurrence.
Alice (eng-sre): followups: 1) postmortem ticket (ENG-8235) assigned to eng-runtime, 2) add a canary perf test to catch p95/p99 regressions in CI, 3) revisit admission control thresholds and safer defaults.
Ben (eng-runtime): I'll add a perf test and a small tweak to the kernel selection fallback to avoid the slow path by default.
Maria (support): closing loop with customer and moving to support ticket, marking as resolved for now. thanks all :thumbsup:
